primary_task: Operate an Aspire distributed application (start/wait/describe/logs/add integrations/deploy) via the Aspire CLI, routing to sub-skills.

requirements.name: aspire
requirements.evidence: operating the AppHost or its resources through the Aspire CLI ... `aspire start --non-interactive --isolated --apphost <path>`; `aspire wait <resource>`
requirements.check: command -v aspire; npm view @microsoft/aspire-cli version; npm view @microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64 version; curl https://registry.npmjs.org/ ; curl https://aspire.dev/install.sh
requirements.observed: absent; npm 13.6.0 (linux-x64 platform package 13.6.0, binary bundled), registry.npmjs.org 200; aspire.dev install script CONNECT 403

requirements.name: dotnet
requirements.check: command -v dotnet; apt-get -s install dotnet-sdk-10.0; curl http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/
requirements.observed: absent; apt simulation resolves dotnet-sdk-10.0 10.0.110 from noble-updates; archive.ubuntu.com 200 (builds.dotnet.microsoft.com CONNECT 403)

requirements.name: aspire.dev
requirements.evidence: `curl -sSL https://aspire.dev/install.sh | bash`; **Always** `aspire docs search <topic>` before editing unfamiliar AppHost APIs

requirements.name: docker
requirements.evidence: resource graph (Postgres / Redis / Rabbit / etc.); Docker Compose deploy target

notes: Aspire CLI installable via npm (one of the listed install alternatives), .NET 10 SDK via Ubuntu apt. Not hard but notable: aspire.dev is blocked (curl install script and possibly `aspire docs search`), and the Docker daemon is unavailable, so AppHosts with container resources (Postgres/Redis...) would not actually run; deploy targets (Azure/AWS/K8s) need cloud accounts but are sub-skill routes. TS AppHosts would need node (available).
